note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Decoupling accuracy and robustness via a self-supervised purifier (GPR-GAE) with convergent multi-step purification

nodes.name: GNNs vulnerable to structural attacks
nodes.description: GNNs rely on the underlying graph structure, so even small structural perturbations can drastically degrade their performance.

nodes.name: Accuracy-robustness trade-off
nodes.description: Defending against attacks requires balancing accuracy on clean data and robustness to adversarial attacks; prioritizing one can harm the other.

nodes.name: Adversarial training decomposes into two terms
nodes.description: The adversarial training objective decomposes into an accuracy term over nodes unaffected by perturbation (weighted by lambda) and a robustness term over affected nodes (weighted by 1-lambda), with the attack budget epsilon controlling lambda (Theorem 3.1).

nodes.name: Adversarial training intertwines conflicting objectives
nodes.description: Adversarial training and robust GNN architectures couple accuracy and robustness in a single model, limiting achievable robustness because higher robustness comes at significant accuracy loss.

nodes.name: Existing purification is heuristic or classifier-dependent
nodes.description: Existing purifiers rely on predefined heuristics (Jaccard pruning, SVD low-rank) or on classifier-derived edge representations, which lack adaptivity and fail to capture structural differences between clean and adversarial edges.

nodes.name: Self-supervised purifier decoupled from classifier
nodes.description: The accuracy objective is assigned to a standard GNN classifier trained on the clean graph, while a separate purifier is trained self-supervised to reconstruct the clean graph G from randomly sampled perturbed graphs G' with a large budget, independent of node labels.

nodes.name: Single-step purification is too coarse
nodes.description: Single-step purification that prunes or keeps edges by fixed criteria makes abrupt, discretized changes, limiting precise recovery under complex or heavy perturbations.

nodes.name: Multi-step purification converges linearly
nodes.description: Under the local Lipschitz assumption induced by the self-supervised objective, iterative purification G(t+1)=G(t)+alpha*dG(t) converges linearly to a stationary point for any step size alpha in (0,1] (Theorem 3.3).

nodes.name: Empirical Lipschitz check supports convergence
nodes.description: The paper empirically estimates the local Lipschitz constant of the one-step purifier on test graphs from 100 random perturbed adjacency pairs to support Theorem 3.3.

nodes.name: Standard GAEs are poor purifiers
nodes.description: Standard GAEs stack static GNN layers that smooth local variations (making adversarially connected nodes similar), suffer oversmoothing for higher-order information, and use proximity-based decoders that reconstruct spurious connections.

nodes.name: GPR-GAE uses multiple GPR filters
nodes.description: GPR-GAE encodes nodes with multiple Generalized PageRank filters whose learnable coefficients weight different adjacency powers, capturing diverse multi-scale structure without oversmoothing.

nodes.name: Edge encoder and order-aware decoder
nodes.description: Edge embeddings are computed from concatenated node embeddings and decoded into directed link scores, which are averaged over both directions for undirected graphs.

nodes.name: Two-part training loss
nodes.description: GPR-GAE is trained with L = L_restore + delta*L_sym, a restoration loss over original edges and injected negative edges plus a symmetry loss, with delta balancing them.

nodes.name: Test-time purification procedure
nodes.description: At test time the adjacency is iteratively updated with step size alpha until ||dA||/||A|| <= tau, and the final continuous (non-discretized) adjacency is passed to the classifier; the paper uses alpha=1, tau=1/1000 and at most 5 steps.

nodes.name: Accuracy improves with each purification step
nodes.description: Classification accuracy improves with each purification step and converges consistently across all alpha values under the termination condition (Fig 2).

nodes.name: State-of-the-art adaptive-attack robustness
nodes.description: Under adaptive attacks GPR-GAE attached to vanilla classifiers achieves higher robustness than vanilla, self-trained, adversarially trained and robust GNN baselines (EvenNet, SoftMedianGDC).

nodes.name: Large gain under severe perturbation
nodes.description: Against PRBCD with epsilon=0.5, adversarially trained GPRGNN reaches 48.5% test accuracy, and GPR-GAE with vanilla GPRGNN improves on this by 15.7 percentage points.

nodes.name: Plug-and-play and clean accuracy preserved
nodes.description: GPR-GAE preserves clean accuracy and works as a plug-and-play defense module compatible with GNN classifiers.

evidence: Sec 3.2: convergence governed by purifier in isolation, decoupling needed

isolated_nodes.name: Datasets and inductive setting
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use Cora, Cora ML, Citeseer, Pubmed, OGB-arXiv and Chameleon in an inductive split with 20 labeled nodes per class, excluding validation and test nodes from training.

isolated_nodes.name: Evasion attack setting
isolated_nodes.description: The work targets evasion (test-time) structural attacks with edge insertions/deletions rather than poisoning attacks.

isolated_nodes.name: Jaccard and SVD purifiers
isolated_nodes.description: Jaccard-GCN prunes edges between nodes with low Jaccard similarity, and SVD-GCN applies a low-rank approximation because attacks affect high-rank components.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from vulnerability and the accuracy-robustness trade-off, through the decomposition of adversarial training, to the decoupled self-supervised purifier, its convergence theory and GPR-GAE design, to test procedure and empirical results.
